name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 21, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at 5:03
p.m., on June 21, 2010, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 18, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 5:06 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ledesma

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

CLOSED SESSION

CS1.  Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6

City Council Minutes  1  June 21, 2010
 CS2. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission
  Viejo v. Saddleback Valley Unified School District (SVUSD), Case No. 00300610

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:07 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session item CS1, the City Council is still
working on the item and will continue the discussion at the end of the meeting. For item CS2,
the Council received an update and there is no reportable action although Council anticipates
reformation of a school ad-hoc committee to help address future issues.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize the Capistrano Valley High School Varsity Boys Swim Team as 2010 CIF
  Southern Section Division I Champion

  Mayor Kelley presented Certificates of Commendation to the coaches and team members
  of the Capistrano Valley High School Swim Team.

P2.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Kelley presented Certificates of Commendation to Corporal Tyler S. Sechrest and
  Lance Corporal Andrew T. Barber-Phillips.

P3.  2-1-1 Awareness Presentation

  The City Council received the presentation from Steve Lemler of Orange County 2-1-1.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

John Maginnis, M.V.: stated that he is a strong supporter of 2-1-1 and he encouraged those in
need of non-emergency health or social services to dial 211 for help.

Larry Maurer, Friends of the Mission Viejo Library Board of Directors, M.V.: provided an
update on the 2010 Readers’ Festival and discussed planning efforts which will ensure that the
event is another community masterpiece and crown jewel.

Dan Avery, M.V.: stated that Mission Viejo’s election costs increased 656% in one year and he
urged residents to get involved.

City Council Minutes  2  June 21, 2010
 Larry Gilbert, M.V.: stated that residents are being asked to give away an extra $8 million dollars
over the life of the contract that is currently being negotiated with Waste Management. He asked
that Council Member Ury refrain from voting on the upcoming contract.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: discussed her attendance at the recent Swim Meet of Champions and
she expressed special pride in our own Chloe Sutton who took home a top award. Mrs.
Bucknum also announced that the Chamber of Commerce is very happy to see that Measure D
was defeated and that the grass-roots campaign was so effective.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 4, 6, 7, 8, 11 and 16 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting of June 7, 2010, as
  amended.

  Amendment: Item 20, page 8, the vote on the second motion listed will be changed to
  reflect a 3-2 vote. Council Members Ledesma and Schlicht were in dissent.

3.  General Municipal Election - November 2, 2010

  (1) Adopted Resolution 10-27 Calling for the Holding of a General Municipal Election to
  be Held on Tuesday, November 2, 2010, for the Election of Certain Officers as Required
  by the Provisions of the Laws of the State of California Relating to General Law; (2)
  adopted Resolution 10-28 Requesting the Board of Supervisors of the County of Orange
  to Consolidate a General Municipal Election to be Held on November 2, 2010, with the
  Statewide General Election to be held on the Date Pursuant to § 10403 of the Elections

City Council Minutes  3  June 21, 2010
   Code; (3) adopted Resolution 10-29 Adopting Regulations for Candidates for Elective
  Office Pertaining to Candidates Statements Submitted to the Voters at an Election to be
  Held on Tuesday, November 2, 2010; and (4) directed the City Clerk to schedule the
  adoption of the resolution citing the election results and the administration of the oath to
  the newly elected Council Members for December 6, 2010, or as soon as possible
  thereafter.

5.  Check Register dated June 4, 2010, in the amount of $697,546.56

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

9.  Cooperative Agreement for the South Orange County Watershed Management
  Area

  (1) Authorized the City Manager to enter into the Cooperative Agreement for the South
  Orange County Watershed Management Area; and (2) approved the 2010-2011 Annual
  Cost-Share Budget for the South Orange County Watershed Management Area.

10.  Destruction of Records - Citywide 2009 Records Purge

  Adopted Resolution 10-31 Authorizing and Directing the City Clerk to Destroy Certain
  City Records and Documents Pursuant to the Government Code of the State of
  California.

12.  City Treasurer's Monthly Report for April 2010

  Received and filed.

13.  Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly Report for April 2010

  Received and filed.

14.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer's Monthly Report for April 2010

  Received and filed.

15.  Authorization for Continuing Appropriations and Preliminary FY 2009-10
  Carryovers

  (1) Adopted Resolution 10-32 to Authorize Appropriations Commencing July 1, 2010,
  Based on Prior Year Spending Levels, Until Such time as the Revised FY 2010-11
  Budget is Adopted; and (2) adopted Resolution 10-33 Authorizing, on an Interim Basis,
  the Carryover of FY 2009-10 Year-End Encumbrances and Periodic Adjustments to the

City Council Minutes  4  June 21, 2010
   FY 2010-11 Budget to Reflect Encumbered FY 2009-10 Balances Until FY 2009-10
  Spending is Closed.

17.  Ratification of Appointment to Solid Waste Ad Hoc Subcommittee

  Designated Councilman Ledesma as the second member of the City Council's Solid
  Waste ad hoc subcommittee.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

18.  Initial Study/Mitigated Negative Declaration for Oso Parkway Widening Project

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  At the hour of 7:01 p.m., Mayor Kelley opened the public hearing. Finding no requests
  to speak, Mayor Kelley closed the public hearing at 7:01 p.m.

  Council Member Schlicht asked for annual reports on traffic accidents at this intersection
  for several years after completion of the project. She noted that if there are too many
  accidents, this might be a good location for a roundabout.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to adopt
  Resolution 10-34 Adopting Mitigated Negative Declaration for Oso Parkway Widening
  Project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

OLD BUSINESS

19.  Revised FY 2010-11 City Budget

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented
  the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  approve the proposed revisions to the FY 2010-11 City Budget.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury

City Council Minutes  5  June 21, 2010
   NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

4.  Check Register dated May 28, 2010, in the amount of $1,664,751.47

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about legal bills for Richards, Watson and Gershon
  and asked if the City has paid invoices for January, February, March and April 2010.

  City Attorney Curley noted that the city is current with its monthly payments.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein indicated
  that the item listed on this check register is for special counsel related to legal issues for
  NPDES permit requirements, which are shared among several cities.

  Council Member Schlicht asked if West Coast Arborists maintains the trees near the
  Marguerite Aquatics Center. She also drew the public’s attention to the payment to ATS
  Communications for commission on cell tower leases.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

6.  Mission Viejo Community Facilities District No 92-1 - Annual Special Tax for Fiscal
  Year 2010-11

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented
  the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht asked if there are any pending foreclosures due to a property
  owner's inability to pay the special tax.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein indicated
  that all of the property owners are current on their taxes.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to

City Council Minutes  6  June 21, 2010
   adopt Resolution 10-30 Establishing an Annual Special Tax for Fiscal Year 2010-11 for
  Community Facilities District No. 92-1 (Mission Viejo Freeway Center).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

7.  Professional Services Agreement for Design and Related Services for the City
  Outlook, Leisure Time and Annual Report

  City Clerk Karen Hamman presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern that we keep finding reasons to award
  contracts to the current vendor and that it sends out the wrong message. If we are looking
  for ways to save money, she feels that this contract should be awarded to the lowest
  bidder even though he is located in Arizona.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht to reject the recommended action and approve
  a contract with Jonathan Price Design. The motion died for lack of a second.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  approve the Professional Services Agreement with brandStrata (A10-21) for design and
  related services for two issues of the bi-annual City Outlook, three issues of the quarterly
  Leisure Time and the 2010 Annual Report in the amount of $34,475.00, through June 30,
  2011.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

8.  Professional Services Consultant Team Contract Amendment

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed concern that one particular vendor gets hundreds of
  thousands of dollars every year from the city and he recommended that the city go out to
  competitive bid for every one of these contracts.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to (1)
  approve the First Amendments to the Contracts for the Professional Services Consultant
  Team (for plan check/design or other professional services); and (2) authorize the City
  Manager to execute the First Amendments.

City Council Minutes  7  June 21, 2010
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

11.  2010 Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 838)

  Council Member Schlicht discussed her earlier communication with Director of Public
  Works Mark Chagnon who said that we are no longer using a particular slurry seal called
  REAS. She asked if the city is compromising safety by not using this slurry seal.

  City Manager Wilberg and City Engineer Rich Schlesinger announced that the REAS has
  been a problem throughout southern California due to material breakdown. Staff
  members have seen several problems in Mission Viejo and have repaired streets where
  the REAS material was used. City staff have therefore chosen to discontinue its use and
  will instead use an alternate material, a type-two TREAS slurry seal.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  approve the bid specifications and authorize staff to advertise for construction bids for the
  2010 Residential Slurry Seal Project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

16.  Fourth Amendment to Agreement for Transit Shelters and Transit Benches - Clear
  Channel Outdoor, Inc.

  Council Member Schlicht asked staff for clarification on the proposals and what was
  disappointing about them.

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson described that the current contract
  with Clear channel provides the city with $67,000 in revenue yet due to the economy,
  Clear Channel’s proposal allowed for only $35,000 in revenue. Accordingly, staff
  recommends extending the current contract for twenty-four months.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1)
  reject all bids; and (2) authorize the City Manager to Sign the Fourth Amendment of
  Agreement with Clear Channel Outdoor, Inc. for Transit Shelters and Transit Benches for
  the Period from June 1, 2010 to June 1, 2012.

City Council Minutes  8  June 21, 2010
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

20.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Kelley announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the OCFA Board so
  she has nothing to report at this time.

21.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

22.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg reminded Council Members and residents of the annual DAWG Walk
which will be held Saturday, June 26, 2010, on the Village Green near the Community
Center. This is a great event that helps to raise money for the Dedicated Animal Welfare Group
and he encouraged residents to attend this event as well as the annual Fourth of July Street Faire.

City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that negotiations are progressing with Waste Management
and he anticipates engaging the Council subcommittee soon. He stated that the negotiations have
been very productive and are advancing in a positive and timely manner.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

23.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

City Council Minutes  9  June 21, 2010
 Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Schlicht

24.  Elimination of Lifetime Healthcare Benefits for the Remaining Eligible Council
  Members

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report and stated that she hopes the Council will
  approve her proposed amendment to the City Council policies.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  approve an Amendment to the Council Policies to Eliminate current and future council
  members from Eligibility in the Mission Viejo Employee Retiree Medical Benefit
  Program.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Ledesma and Schlicht
  NOES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  ABSENT:  None

Council Member Schlicht stated that there is a lot of misinformation circulating about Measure D
and there was no way the proponents could compete against $130,000 in special interests money.
She read a paragraph from the Orange County Business Journal on Measure D and the Orange
County Fair Grounds Measure and stated that Mission Viejo voters were bamboozled. She
stated that we are a great community but we are built out so measure D proponents are concerned
about the community being built up. Council Member Schlicht invited residents to the
Saddleback Republican Assembly’s Independence Day TEA Party on Marguerite Parkway near
the intersection of Olympiad. It will be held on July 4, 2010, from 7:00 p.m. to 8:30 p.m.,
followed by the city’s fireworks show. She also encouraged nature lovers to visit the web site
http://www.starrranch.org where, right now, viewers can watch baby owls being hatched.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury stated that people who voted to oppose Measure D were not bamboozled.
Instead, they came out to understand the issue and the bamboozling part was called the Right to
Vote Initiative. He noted that comparing the vote on the fair grounds to the vote in Mission
Viejo doesn’t work. There are realtors who do business in town who opposed the measure and
people should reflect on whether we are going to be governed by the fear of what might happen,
verses the reality of the decisions the City Council is making. Council Member Ury stated that
he would like to see the supporters of Measure D put some money on the line and then revisit the
issue in ten years to see if their fears have come to fruition. He stated that the voters rejected the
measure so highly because they understood that there was nothing nefarious going on. Council
Member Ury expressed disappointment that he was unable to attend the Nadadores event since

City Council Minutes  10  June 21, 2010
 he was out of town attending a softball showcase with his daughter. He congratulated the
participants and the award-winners and stated that he hopes to make it to the next event.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness announced that he and his family spent Father's Day exploring the Oso
Creek Trail. They started on the trail head at Olympiad and Jeronimo and they hiked to the end
of the trail at Marguerite Parkway. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness noted that this is a fantastic
community asset and he enjoyed his time discovering all that the trail has to offer.

Mayor Kelley

25.  Pension Reform

  Mayor Kelley presented her report and stated that it's time that we, as a city, take action
  on this issue and become a leader among cities in Orange County and elsewhere in
  California.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to direct staff to
  research alternatives to our current retirement program, to develop a proposal for a
  second tier retirement benefit program and to report back within 90 days.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

Mayor Kelley discussed the Swim Meet of Champions which was held this past weekend and
announced that she was pleased to attend the event twice to present medals. She was really taken
with the excellence of the Nadadores swim organization and the way they represent Mission
Viejo not only in the county but in the nation and the world. She also discussed her attendance at
the first and last classes of the recent Parent Project series. She heard overwhelming responses
about this program which addresses issues that parents experience with their teenagers. Mayor
Kelley recognized and thanked the Sheriff’s Deputies who teach this course and she reiterated
what a wonderful program it is. Mayor Kelley stated that she neglected to make an appointment
to the Transportation Corridor System (TCS) in January. This is a committee that used to meet
frequently and while they no longer convene on a regular basis, there may be a need at some
point in time. She announced that she has also received a request from Council member Ury
whose work schedule has not allowed him to attend the Foothill/Eastern TCA meetings.
Because the year is half over, Mayor Kelley appointed herself to serve as the representative to
the Foothill/Eastern TCA and to the TCS and she appointed Mayor Pro Tem Leckness to serve as
alternate for both boards. She asked Council Member Ledesma if he wished to be removed from
the GMA 9 Board or if he had just had some recent conflicts.

City Council Minutes  11  June 21, 2010
 City Manager Wilberg announced that there will only be one more meeting of the GMA 9 group
and Council Member Ledesma indicated that he will complete his service on the board.

Mayor Kelley mentioned that the Dedicated Animal Welfare Group (DAWG) will hold its dog
walk and pet fair on Saturday, June 26, 2010, from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. The event takes
place at Oso Park next to the Murray Center. This is not only a fundraiser but it’s a fun event for
the community and pet owners. She also reminded residents to mark their calendars for the
Mission Viejo Activities Committee Fourth of July Street Faire which is held from noon until the
end of the fireworks show. Council Member Ury and Mayor Pro Tem Leckness have
courageously volunteered to sit in the dunk tank and she will also be working at the event.
Mayor Kelley encouraged residents to volunteer and she noted that Mission Viejo puts on the
best fireworks display in the area. She also announced that she serves on the Orange County
Parks Commission and they had a rather historic meeting this last Thursday when the Parks
Commission recommended acceptance of a donation of 20,000 acres of open space from the
Irvine Company. This will create many new opportunities for those who enjoy the outdoors and
she will have more information as the proposal moves forward.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 8:47 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session to further discuss
item CS1. The City Council reconvened at 9:56 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was nothing to report from Closed Session.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:58 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of Dan Levine to Tuesday, July 6, 2010, at 5:00
p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of July 6, 2010

City Council Minutes  12  June 21, 2010
